title: Frequency-varying interaural discordance did not establish added hearing-trouble prediction across independent NHANES samples
abstract: A source-frozen weighted logistic model trained in 3,816 NHANES 2011–2012 adults was evaluated in 4,263 separately sampled 2015–2016 adults aged 20–69. Adding the centered root-mean-square right-minus-left threshold difference across seven frequencies to demographic and standard audiometric summaries changed target log loss by -0.00006701 (95% conditional stratified-PSU bootstrap interval -0.00019149 to 0.00006265; source-and-target refit interval -0.00054416 to 0.00086051). Target AUROC changed by 0.000187; source grouped cross-validation worsened. Stable incremental prediction of self-reported hearing trouble was not established. This is a negative representation test in complete-case public survey participants, not evidence of no physiological information in interaural asymmetry.
